correctness.rationale: The exact Gaussian modal transition Y_j^+=cos(jT)Y_j+sin(jT)ξ_j gives Hermite-quadratic eigenvalues ρ_j=E cos²(jT), γ_ij=E cos(iT)cos(jT). Cauchy–Schwarz bounds every |γ_ij| by ρ*=max_jρ_j and hence maximizes IACT at ρ*. Nonnegative Fejér-square identity for N=K+1 forces max_j E cos(2jT)≥−1/K. Uniform nontrivial N-th roots with T=mπ/N attain the bound while satisfying E T=π/2; saturation forces all c_j=−1/K, grid support, symmetric weights 1/K by discrete Fourier inversion and the listed antisymmetric mean constraint. For K≤3 the constraint kills all antisymmetric degrees, while for K≥4 there are nonzero feasible small perturbations. Boundary K=1 yields IACT=1, and persistent modes are assigned infinity. The source verifier code and analytic argument were inspected; finite K=1..18 spectral diagnostics do not prove the universal bound.
